messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard error (the “standard deviation” of the null‑hypothesis sampling distribution)**  

For a one‑sample test the standard error of the sample mean is

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
* \(s = 1.4\) (sample standard deviation)  
* \(n = 40\) (sample size)

\[
SE = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.221
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test (i.e., the standard error of the mean) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is s / sqrt(n). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null hypothesis. That would be population standard deviation? But we only have sample standard deviation. So we can approximate using sample standard deviation: SE = s / sqrt(n) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. So SE ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2214. So standard deviation of the null hypothesis test (i.e., standard error) is about 0.221.

Alternatively, if they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? The test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (s / sqrt(n)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the null distribution of t is sqrt(n-1)/(sqrt(n-1))? Actually t distribution has variance n-1/(n-3) for df>2. But maybe they want the standard error.

Thus answer: approx 0.221.

We can also compute the p-value using the function. But they didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation of null hypothesis test. So answer: 0.221.
